frontier.hypothesis: The three orphaned spill pseudos are a CODE_LABEL-placement artifact of the loop's own exit/continue label, so the lever is the loop's exit topology and not the exit test's arithmetic.
frontier.mechanism: combine.c:10834 emits `(use (reg))` only after the note-placement scan hits a CODE_LABEL without finding a referencing insn (combine.c:10826). mips.md:2346 makes the ashift pair that creates the fold unavoidable, and the target's build paid the same fold and still got vars=80, so the difference is where the notes could land, i.e. which CODE_LABEL `tem` is.
frontier.next_probe: Read tmp/grind/func_80070C70/dumps/text1b.combine for the insn immediately preceding each `(use (reg 116/168/173))` - in the s9 dumps they sit after insns 203, 544 and 405 - and identify the CODE_LABEL `tem` resolves to, cross-reading jump.c's duplicate_loop_exit_test (jump.c:2163-2258) for which label it creates. Then attack THAT label from C: what statement ends the loop body (call vs store), whether the increment is written in the for-header or at the bottom of the body, and what immediately follows the loop.

frontier.hypothesis: The top-test chassis is now the shorter road: its deficit is one structural fix (the 24 frame bytes) where the do/while chassis needs the whole cse_set_around_loop hoist that s7 and s8 measured unreachable on a do/while.
frontier.mechanism: s9's classify run quantifies both residuals. The do/while's is a 6-shape PRE-RA difference that is exactly the missing hoist; the top-test's is 13 frame shapes plus one instruction. Score ranks them 39 vs 49 only because the frame overshoot inflates 13 otherwise-correct insns.
frontier.next_probe: Work the F12 label-topology probe on memory/grind/func_80070C70/chassis-toptest-shapeexact-49.c, and stop spending sessions trying to import the cse structure onto the do/while body. Any hit there should be re-classified with goal_from_tgt.py rather than judged on score alone.

frontier.hypothesis: IconC70's trailing 24 bytes have a real member list that the placeholder `s16 sp50[12]` only approximates, and recovering it is a prerequisite for any submission (carried from s1/s2/s3, still unspent).
frontier.mechanism: Correctness of the submitted C, not codegen - the 0x20 SIZE is proven twice (frame arithmetic in s1, the BB2_FRAME_DEBUG census in s6) but the field list is not evidence-backed.
frontier.next_probe: Read the $a1-relative stores in func_80069898's other callers (func_8006B120, func_8006CFBC, func_800720FC, func_80074488, func_8006F97C) and build the true field list; propagate the corrected type to func_8006F97C's ledger, which is an active queue sibling in the same TU.
